title: Dutar (two-string long-neck lute)
summary: The dutar is a long-necked lute of Central Asia whose name means two strings. A slim pear-shaped body of mulberry wood runs into a very long neck with tied-on gut frets. The strings are played with the fingers, in quick rhythmic patterns or long, singing lines.
howToPlay: Two strings run along the long neck, the lower on the left. Each lane marks the fret where a note is played.
A bead slides down the string to its fret. Pluck the lane as the bead lands.
Open lanes at the top sound the string without pressing.
Try the caravan line first, then the quick tapping, then the slow sigh.
rules: The notes come from a seven-note scale starting on A, in two octaves.
Every phrase is played through twice.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra plucks cost points.
The slow sigh has three beats to the bar; the others have two or four.
heritageNote: Two-string lutes like the dutar have been played across Central Asia for centuries, by singers and poets who accompanied their own verses. Makers still tie the gut frets by hand so that each player can tune the scale to taste.
